newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January consumer prices up 1.96 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January consumer prices up 1.96 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's January consumer price index rose 1.96 percent compared to January 1996, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Wednesday.
January's consumer price index rise was well below an average forecast of 3.18 percent compiled through Monday's poll of Taiwan economists.
The economists had calculated that an average 9.0 percent increase in state-controlled oil prices promulgated on January 1 would add some 0.387 percentage points to the total.
The directorate's official report on the inflation figures did not give a breakdown for the extent of the impact of the oil price hike.
January food prices fell 2.15 percent from December due to abundant supplies in the current peak season for vegetables, the directorate said.
Prices for clothing were down 4.48 percent.
Import prices declined 5 percent from a year earlier, while export prices were down 3.04 percent.-Taipei Newsroom(5080815)
